`get_submission_arguments()` identifies arguments in each submission.
`group_submission_arguments()` separately groups and counts them
once complete submission text is available. It builds on the workflow in the
[prosecutor consultation analysis](https://werk.statt.codes/posts/2026-09-17-Prosecutor-Submission/).
This first draft uses [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) for provider access
and structured output. The optional dependency, explicit namespace calls,
roxygen documentation and offline tests follow the development practices in
[R Packages](https://r-pkgs.org/).

## Set up a model

Install ellmer separately. Choose a provider/model with structured output
support and access through your provider account.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("ellmer")
```

Store the provider's key in your user or project `.Renviron`, then restart R.
For example, the file can contain `OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key-here`. Anthropic uses
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; Google Gemini uses `GOOGLE_API_KEY`. Follow ellmer's
documentation for other providers. Keep credential files out of version control.
ParlAT does not read, modify or return those files or the key.

If you already use a `.env` file, explicitly load it into the R process first:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# Requires the optional dotenv package, installed separately.
dotenv::load_dot_env(".env")
```

## Prepare full text

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ParlAT)

submissions <- get_consultation_submissions(
  "/gegenstand/XXVIII/ME/44", include_text = TRUE
)
```

`submission_text` contains inline text only. Review the `documents` list-column:
when there are attachments, the inline text may just be a cover letter. Prepare
the complete text, including PDF extraction or OCR as appropriate, in one
character column. Keep exactly one row per submission with a unique
`submission_id`. Combine multiple documents belonging to the same submission
before analysis. Restrict each run to one consultation.

The first draft does not download PDFs, run OCR, or decide whether an attachment
duplicates inline text. Missing text remains visible as `missing_text` and is
excluded from the analysed denominator.

## Extract, group and count

This example assumes `submission_text` has been reviewed and completed. Use
`text_column = "full_text"` if you store prepared text in a separate column.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
arguments <- get_submission_arguments(
  submissions,
  model = "openai/gpt-4.1-mini",
  direction = "both"
)

result <- group_submission_arguments(
  arguments, model = "openai/gpt-4.1-mini", n_groups = 5
)

result$submissions
result$arguments
result$groups
result$frequencies
result$direction_frequencies
saveRDS(result, "consultation-arguments.rds")
```

`n_groups` is an upper limit across the corpus, including any residual group.
It does not limit the number of arguments extracted from a submission. The
model may form fewer groups if the material warrants fewer.

The workflow sends one extraction request per non-empty submission, one request
to define groups from all distinct argument descriptions, and one assignment
request per batch (50 descriptions by default). Every request uses a fresh chat.
No additional paid probe request is sent. The functions make real provider
requests and can incur charges; start with a small subset. Provider libraries
may retry requests according to their own policies.

`arguments` retains a submission identifier and verbatim source quotations for
each argument. Each occurrence has its own argument ID. Exact duplicate
descriptions and directions across submissions share an assignment request.
Similar descriptions with different wording can fall in the same group but
remain separate registry entries. Quotations must occur in the supplied source;
the check cannot establish whether the interpretation is correct.

Extraction accepts one or several submissions and preserves their identifiers.
Save `arguments` to rerun grouping with a different model or group limit without
repeating extraction. Direction is relative to the proposal or provision:
`direction = "pro"`, `"contra"` or `"both"`. One submission can contain both.
Topics are shared across directions; `direction_frequencies` reports pro/contra
counts separately. Overall topic totals count a submission once even when it
raises both pro and contra arguments.

## Interpret the frequencies

For each group:

- `n_arguments` counts extracted argument occurrences across submissions.
- `n_submissions` counts distinct submissions raising at least one argument in
  the group. Several arguments in one submission count once here.
- `proportion` divides `n_submissions` by all successfully analysed submissions,
  including those returning zero arguments.

For example, if three submissions are analysed and two raise a cost argument,
the cost group's proportion is `2 / 3`, even if the third submission contains
no relevant argument. A fourth submission with missing text is excluded from
that denominator. A submission can raise arguments in several groups, so group
proportions need not sum to one.

## Failures and review

By default, any extraction failure stops the call. With `on_error = "continue"`,
failed extractions are marked `failed`, with `n_arguments = NA`, and excluded
from the denominator. They are never treated as successful zero-argument
responses. Inspect `result$submissions` before interpreting frequencies.
Group-definition or assignment failures always stop the call; a partial
assignment cannot silently become a valid frequency table. Unknown, duplicate
or omitted IDs are rejected.

`max_input_chars` guards the size of each source input. It is not a token budget
and does not account for the model's context-window rules. Inputs are never
silently truncated. All distinct descriptions must fit into the codebook
request; for large corpora, use a suitable context window or reduce the corpus.

Review the codebook, source quotations, and missing/failed cases before using
the counts. Model outputs vary, and this helper does not validate political
interpretations. Save results and record your model and settings. This draft
does not provide durable checkpoints, automatic resume, hierarchical grouping,
cost estimates, or automatic PDF/OCR preparation.
